title: Mixed-Integer Programming for Change-point Detection
contribution: Replaces the segment-assignment block of the two existing contiguous-segmentation MIPs for piecewise-linear change-point detection with nested cumulative binaries whose LP relaxation projects integrally onto the assignment variables, proves both benchmarks non-integral, and shows faster global solves on 375 of 600 stock-price settings (arXiv v2, retitled 'Change-Point Detection via Piecewise Linear Fitting Using MIP').
problem_entry: Existing PWL-fitting MIPs (Goldberg et al. 2021 'Basic', Rebennack-Krasko 2020 'Alternative') have weak LP relaxations with fractional segment assignments that cause excessive branch-and-bound effort, and statistical penalization methods cannot handle continuous fits or shared multi-dimensional segmentation (pp. 1-4).
key_idea: Swap only the assignment block: X_{j,t}=1 iff t is in the first j segments, nested and monotone, with delta as differences; the block is TU, so its projection is integral, and it plugs into both base models unchanged (pp. 7-11).
assumptions: 1-D domain, mostly uniform time index; fixed K (or upper bound with l0 penalty); l1/l2 loss; data-driven parameter box and big-M copied from Rebennack-Krasko; continuity optional (bilinear or linearized); no continuity in the multi-dimensional case; DP alternative for the discontinuous case acknowledged but not run (pp. 3, 5-10, 18-19).
proof_devices: TU by rows with at most two opposite-sign nonzeros plus identity block, then integral projection (Prop. 1, Cor. 1, pp. 10-11)

total-variation invariant TV(delta_j) <= 2 on the extended projection vs an oscillating fractional point feasible for the Basic LPR (Lemma 1, Prop. 2, pp. 11-12; feasibility completion App. C, pp. 20-21)
fractional extreme point of the Alternative block certified by 24 linearly independent tight constraints (Prop. 3, pp. 12-13)
contiguity by backward propagation of non-contiguity to segment 1 (Remark 1, p. 6)
feasible-region equivalence/strict containment with explicit unused-segment counterexample, and coincidence of optimal (m,c,yhat) by segment splitting (Remarks 3-5, pp. 8-9)
experiments: Gurobi 13.0.2, Apple M3, single thread, 3 seeds, 2000 s limit, minimal tuning, code+outputs on GitHub; yfinance stock prices; 600 settings (T up to 500, K up to 6, D up to 10); win counts (Extended 375/600) and cumulative runtime with time-outs at 2000 s (171,884 s vs 216,380 s and 246,307 s); Basic wins 42/100 in continuity-l1 and Extended is not lowest in multi-dimensional l2 cumulative time; no detection-accuracy evaluation (pp. 14-16, 22-24).
positioning: Positions against non-contiguous (Bertsimas-Shioda), fixed-grid (Toriello-Vielma), non-global (Cui et al.) and penalization methods; builds directly on the PWL MIP line and uses Warwicker-Rebennack to pick the benchmark; hedges with own non-monotonicity paper (Shah, Dey, Molinaro 2026) (pp. 2-3, 10, 13).
writing: Three-bullet contributions, change-point vs breakpoint terminology note, named formulations, Remarks for feasibility relations, explicit caveat that polyhedral strength is not conclusive for run time; superlatives ('consistently') stronger than the tables in places (pp. 1-2, 6-9, 13, 15-16).
limits_future: Future: decomposition for scalability, online variants (p. 16); unstated: small T (<=500, <=180 with continuity), big-M blocks untouched, Extended Alternative relaxes Alternative's feasible region, no DP baseline, single data family (pp. 4-5, 8-10, 14).

method_links.note: IP-style joint convexification of a recurring substructure (assignment block) via an extended formulation with integral projection, inside formulations that also carry bilinear continuity constraints
positive integrality result paired with non-integrality of both benchmarks via explicit points and an explicit caveat that LP strength is not conclusive for run time
no ground-truth ceiling or stripped instrument; full Gurobi, run time only, single thread and three seeds
deliverable is a globally optimal fit reached faster, not a cheap relaxation used as the certificate

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: X_{j,t} nested vectors with delta as differences; Prop. 1 TU proof; modular swap into two formulations

transferable: Nested cumulative binaries with delta_{j,t} = X_{j,t} - X_{j-1,t} and two monotonicity families, proved TU by opposite-sign two-nonzero rows plus identity block (pp. 7-11)
Separate two projected LP relaxations by a functional bounded on one (total variation) and an explicit violating point of the other, with the feasible completion in an appendix (pp. 11-12, 20-21)
Certify a fractional vertex by n linearly independent tight constraints that determine it uniquely (pp. 12-13)
Modular block swap into each competing formulation for a clean 2x2 comparison (pp. 8, 14)
Report instance-wise win counts and cumulative time with time-outs charged at the limit; single thread, three seeds, minimal tuning, released code and raw outputs (pp. 14-16)

quotes.text: We establish that the projection of the linear programming relaxation onto the space of these extended segment-assignment variables is integral, yielding a tighter relaxation.

As a result, the polyhedral comparisons in this section are not necessarily conclusive with respect to overall computational performance (also see Shah et al. [2026]), which is therefore assessed empirically in Section 4.

title: Asymptotically tight Lagrangian dual of smooth nonconvex problems via improved error bound of Shapley-Folkman Lemma
contribution: Gives a face-dimension proof of the Shapley-Folkman Lemma, a refined error bound by randomized rounding, and the first bound under which the nonconvexity of a Minkowski sum vanishes as the number of summands grows (smooth hidden convex components at extreme points), yielding asymptotic tightness of the Lagrangian dual of block-structured smooth nonconvex problems with sparsity constraints.
problem_entry: Strong duality of the Lagrangian dual of a block-structured nonconvex program needs only convexity of the image set P in (objective, constraint) space; classical Shapley-Folkman bounds on its nonconvexity do not vanish, so ask whether they can vanish as k grows (pp. 1-5).
key_idea: Write each point of conv(sum A_i) as a sum of faces with total dimension <= n, round the few nonzero-dimensional pieces randomly (variances add), and absorb the error into the growing sum of smooth convex 'hidden components' (balls) at extreme points; epigraphs of L-smooth functions supply balls of radius 1/L, carried through B by a projection factor (pp. 8-23).
assumptions: OPT_L = DUAL (regularity, pathological cases excluded); conv(A_i) closed and pointed; bounded inner radius Xi <= beta; f 1-coercive, closed, proper, f(0) finite, L-smooth; projection factor L_s(B) >= omega > 0 (needs s >= m, generic); smoothness can be local (pp. 8-9, 19, 21-23). Reader notes: Theorem 6 bounds DUAL between OPT(b+E1)-E and OPT(b), so the gap vanishes only with continuity of OPT in b, not discussed; Claims 5-6 call f convex though only the quadratic upper bound is used (pp. 21-23).
proof_devices: gap formula Delta <= E + OPT(b) - OPT(b+E1) via primal characterization of the Lagrangian dual (Theorem 3, pp. 8-9)
face-dimension reduction: rank-nullity directions summing to zero, move until a relative boundary, pointedness (Claims 1-2, Lemma 4, pp. 10-11)
face heredity of inner radius Xi(A cap F) <= Xi(A) (Claim 4, p. 11)
Caratheodory distribution with variance <= Xi^2 and additive variances under independence, existence by averaging (Lemmas 5-6, p. 12; Theorem 4, p. 13)
L-smooth squared gauge of the hidden-component sum applied to random rounding error (Lemma 7, pp. 15-16; Theorem 5, p. 16)
explicit inscribed ball of radius 1/L in the epigraph of an L-smooth function (Claim 5, p. 21) and inscribed ball of an ellipsoid via singular-value ratio (Lemma 11, Claim 6, p. 22)
closedness/pointedness of conv(epi) by 1-coercivity and a pigeonhole on a Caratheodory representation; Rockafellar Thm 9.1 for linear images (Lemmas 8-10, pp. 19-20)
necessity examples: {0,1}^n singletons (p. 14), l1-ball hollow persists vs p>1 (Remark 2, p. 17), components needed only at extreme points (Remark 3, p. 17)
positioning: Starr 1969 -> optimization duality-gap uses (Aubin-Ekeland, Bertsekas et al., Udell-Boyd) -> refinements (Bi-Tang, Kerdreux et al., Nguyen-Vohra) and a discrete analogue (Murota-Tamura); claims first vanishing bound; image-convexity view linked to S-Lemma/Dines and hidden convexity; own Lagrangian-dual papers as context (pp. 2-4, 8, 11, 23-25).
writing: Abstract poses a yes/no geometric question and answers it affirmatively; dual optimization/economics framing; informal main application in the intro; one-sentence key-insight flag; a Remark with figure-backed example per hypothesis; no conclusion section; typos remain in v2 (pp. 1-5, 13, 17).
limits_future: Theory only; non-pursued extensions are p-th power gauges/other measures (Remark 1, p. 17) and local smoothness (Remark 5, p. 23); no rate for the gap itself, no tightness examples for Theorems 4-6, no computation of how large k must be; paper ends without a conclusion (p. 23).

method_links.note: conditions under which the cheap decomposable Lagrangian dual bound becomes asymptotically exact for smooth nonconvex blocks
each hypothesis demarcated by a failure example (singletons, l1 balls, missing components at extreme points); no tight example for the bounds themselves
convexity read off a local substructure (hidden convex components at extreme points), but with convex-geometry/probability tools rather than MILP closures
no solver habit to explain; question posed from the foundational standing of a classical lemma, practice only as motivation

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Lemmas 5-7 bound distances by expected squared error with additive variances

transferable: Turn any bound on image-set nonconvexity Phi(P) into a duality-gap bound via Delta <= Phi(P) + OPT(b) - OPT(b + Phi(P) 1) (Theorem 3, pp. 8-9)
Face-dimension counting plus a kernel-direction move to prove Shapley-Folkman/Caratheodory-type statements (Claims 1-2, Lemma 4, pp. 10-11)
Random rounding with additive variances, then absorb the error into a growing convex body whose squared gauge is L-smooth (Lemmas 5-7, pp. 12-16)
Explicit ball of radius 1/L inside the epigraph of an L-smooth function through every graph point (Claim 5, p. 21)
Projection factor (singular-value ratio over column subsets) to carry a ball through a sparse linear map (Def. 6, Claim 6, pp. 20-22)
Show a smoothness hypothesis is needed with a two-point set plus k p-norm balls, hollow persists for p = 1 (Remark 2, p. 17)

quotes.text: Is it possible for the nonconvexity of the Minkowski sum of n-dimensional nonconvex sets to vanish asymptotically, rather than merely converge to a constant, as the number of summands increases?

To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing an asymptotically vanishing nonconvexity measure for Minkowski sums of nonconvex sets within the framework of the Shapley–Folkman Lemma.
